drop_dates.2025-12-13: Warren Haynes Christmas Jam. An all-Bob-Dylan covers tribute set that sits in the archive.org 'moe' collection because moe. members guested. It is not a moe. concert, and several copies of the tape are uploaded under a 'bob' identifier -- the same recording, mislabelled, more than once.
drop_dates.2022-02-24: Everyone Orchestra (Matt Butler). An improv all-star jam featuring Derhak and Schnier. Nothing played that night is evidence about what moe. plays at a moe. show.
drop_dates.2025-10-31: Halloween. The band played MONTY PYTHON: 'JAMALOT', 'Ni!', 'Brave Sir Robin', 'Camelot', 'Bring Out Your Dead', 'Icky Icky Icky', 'Monk's Chant'. Those are bits, not songs, and they were sitting in the vocabulary as things moe. might play next week. The real songs buried in that set (Meat, Rebubula, The Pit) are lost with it, and that is the right trade: a costume show is not evidence about an ordinary Tuesday, and its fake titles poison the vocabulary for every show that is.

moe2024-06-14.why: moe. did not play on 2024-06-14; the show does not exist. This is set two of 2025-06-14. The taper's own description reads 'June 14 2025'; the artwork file is named Northlands25_1500x787+sm.jpg; it was uploaded 2025-07-10, four weeks after the 2025 show and thirteen months after the date it claims; setlist.fm has no moe. show on 2024-06-14 and one on 2025-06-14; and its six tracks (07-12: Okayalright, Seat of My Pants, Puebla into Timmy Tucker, Space Truckin', Opium, It) map exactly onto slots 7-13 of the 2025-06-14 setlist, in order. The description says 'set two', which is why the tracks start at 07. Note the counter-example: moe2023-02-25.ca14.flac16 has the same symptom -- a year mismatch between its date and its description -- and is NOT mis-dated. The taper typo'd their own notes. Same tell, opposite answer, which is why an entry here has to carry more than the tell.

junk_patterns.why: Artists moe. covers, written by the taper in place of (or beside) the song itself: the annotation arrives where the title should be, so the artist's name lands in the vocabulary as a moe. song. This is a DROP rather than a tag because nothing was performed under this name -- the parser found a credit, not an entry. Grows as new ones surface in review. No counter-example is listed because none of the 304 titles comes near any of these names, and lint warns on every run if that ever changes.

Band-member surnames. Tapers write them beside a sit-in or a solo credit -- 'Rob Derhak just vocals' -- and the credit becomes a song. Safe to drop outright because no moe. title contains one; lint holds this against the vocabulary, the aliases and the protected titles on every run, so the day that stops being true it says so.

gear_patterns.why: A lineage-line token from the old parser's gear list. What it stands for is not recorded anywhere I could read -- not in the source it came from, not in the corpus notes -- so this entry says only what is known: it appeared in taper lineage preambles for this band and was filtered there. It is a three-letter all-caps token, which is the exact shape that got ATL and NYC deleted, so it lives in a pack where lint can hold it against a real vocabulary instead of in code that ships to bands nobody has checked it against.

As 'kcy': a lineage token carried over from the old gear list with no recorded expansion. Filtered here because a taper preamble is not a setlist, and kept out of the generic filter because I cannot say it is safe for a band I have never seen.

acoustic_patterns.why: moe.'s own billing for an acoustic night: Al and Rob as a duo, dot optional, since tapers write it both ways. Matched on the BRAND name and never on the bare word 'acoustic' -- tapers list their gear in the description, 'percussion, MalletKat, flute, acoustic guitar' is not an acoustic show, and matching the bare word swept in New Year's Eve and six other full electric nights. This matters because a duo plays the same songs shorter: one song that runs 18.8 minutes electric runs 6.4 acoustic, so pooling the two averages distributions that have nothing to do with each other. A tagged night is left out of every length distribution and stays in the corpus for everything else.
